[Lesson 04 / Exponential evolution]{.lesson-kicker}

# Let each wave decay exactly

[Once a PDE becomes independent scalar ODEs, why approximate an evolution we can solve?]{.lesson-deck}

[First six experiments · 6 of 6](../../start/index.qmd){.lesson-route-label}

:::

Fourier differentiation made the spatial operator exact for our cosine
mode, but [forward Euler](../fourier/index.qmd) left a time error. Constant
diffusivity gives us another option: solve the equation of each Fourier
coefficient analytically. The resulting implementation is a transform,
a multiplication, and an inverse transform.

The forward/multiply/backward pattern keeps the mathematical update visible.
Compare its exact linear multiplier with the implicit approximation in
[backward-Euler heat](../implicit-euler/index.qmd).

## Solve the coefficient equation

For $\partial_tu=D\Delta u$ on the periodic box, every represented mode
satisfies

$$
\frac{d\widehat u_{\mathbf{k}}}{dt}
=-D|\mathbf{k}|^2\widehat u_{\mathbf{k}}.
$$ {#eq-mode}

Separation of variables gives

$$
\widehat u_{\mathbf{k}}(t+\Delta t)
=e^{-D|\mathbf{k}|^2\Delta t}\widehat u_{\mathbf{k}}(t).
$$ {#eq-exponential}

The multiplier lies in $[0,1]$ for $D,\Delta t>0$. At $\mathbf{k}=0$ it
is one, preserving the mean. Unlike Euler's multiplier
$1-D|\mathbf{k}|^2\Delta t$, it cannot amplify a high-frequency mode.

For $u(\mathbf{x},0)=1+0.2\cos x\cos y\cos z$, @eq-exponential gives
the same $e^{-3Dt}$ decay as the continuous solution. This special initial
condition is fully represented by the Fourier grid, so both spatial and
temporal truncation errors vanish; roundoff remains.

## Build the propagator once

The FFT's real-space and Fourier-space decompositions can differ. Use the
Fourier outbox, rather than assuming a local index is a global wavenumber:

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="propagator" dedent=4}
```

`for_each_kpoint` supplies physical wavenumbers, including spacing and
frequency ordering. The vectors contain only the modes owned by this
rank. The propagator depends on the fixed timestep and diffusivity, so
we calculate it once.

Now advance the field:

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="evolve" dedent=4}
```

OpenPFC's inverse FFT already supplies the normalization needed for a
forward/backward round trip. Dividing by the global cell count again
would destroy the mean: the conservation check would catch that mistake.

## Compare three answers to one problem

| Method | Spatial action | One-step mode multiplier |
|:--|:--|:--|
| FD + Euler | Second-order periodic stencil | $1+D\Delta t\lambda_h$ |
| Fourier + Euler | Exact symbol on represented modes | $1-D\Delta t|\mathbf{k}|^2$ |
| Fourier + exponential | Exact symbol on represented modes | $e^{-D\Delta t|\mathbf{k}|^2}$ |

: Three deliberately small numerical choices. Here $\lambda_h$ is the FD Laplacian eigenvalue derived in lesson 2. {#tbl-methods}

![RMS continuum errors of the three implementations for N=16, D=1, and dt=0.001. The exponential method's remaining error is roundoff; it is not zero in floating-point arithmetic.](../figures/methods.svg){#fig-methods}

The existing backward-Euler diffusion example would use
$1/(1+D\Delta t|\mathbf{k}|^2)$. It is stable for linear diffusion but
still has a temporal truncation error. Stability and exact integration
are different properties.

## Run it and test the idea

From `examples/heat/exponential`:

```sh
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --source-root .. --launcher=none
```

The source is [model.cpp](model.cpp), with [input.json](input.json) for
parameters. As before, inspect `results/diagnostics.csv` and the final
rank fields inside the attempt directory printed by the CLI.

Change to `dt=0.1` and `steps=1`. This advances to the same final time
as 100 steps of size 0.001, with a result still close to the exact
solution. Compare their errors: taking more FFT round trips can accumulate
more roundoff. An exact mathematical propagator does not make repeated
floating-point computation exact.

As a deliberate counterexample, replace the exponential multiplier by
$1-D|\mathbf{k}|^2\Delta t$ and keep the large timestep. Predict which
high-frequency modes amplify. The executable's exponential path has no
Euler stability guard, so this edited experiment needs its own stability
analysis.

## Where exact propagation ends

Variable diffusivity couples modes. Nonlinear terms such as $u^3$ do too.
Applying @eq-exponential to the linear part alone does not integrate the
whole nonlinear PDE exactly. Exponential time-differencing methods extend
the idea by approximating the remaining contribution; Cox and Matthews
develop higher-order schemes for stiff systems [@cox2002]. That is the
bridge to OpenPFC's existing nonlinear spectral and ETD examples, rather
than a claim that this short program implements a general ETD solver.

The numerical checks compare every cell with the independent cosine-mode
solution, verify mean preservation and decay, and run on one and two
ranks. General initial data still have Fourier truncation error; no
nonperiodic or variable-coefficient case is qualified by these checks.

The complete [C++ model](model.cpp) and [starting input](input.json)
are available with this lesson. It also uses the shared [lesson.hpp](../lesson.hpp);
keep its relative location when saving the files.
